correctness.rationale: All claims were reconstructed from definitions; clique fiber omitted multiplicities and witness translation are exact for every finite simple G and m>=2; cyclic word avoidance, transfer trace, upper bound and odd/even counts have complete case proofs in RESULT.md. Independent direct enumeration checks 86 labeled graph profiles and 15 cyclic base orders; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The exact product work covers scalar minimum numbers or inequalities; the counting paper counts minimum super dominating sets of ordinary graph classes; the 2023 product paper treats other domination variants. None of the inspected claims logically supplies the weighted all-set equality for arbitrary clique-blowup bases without proving the missing correspondence.

originality.rationale: Checked 2017 lexicographic-product super-domination work, 2022 enumeration work, and 2017 OEIS base-cycle irredundance records. Published results include general scalar bounds and the original cycle counts, but the exact all-configuration super domination ↔ base irredundance correspondence for all clique blowups and its full weighted polynomial were not found. Unindexed equivalent formulations remain a priority risk; known cycle data are not claimed independently new.
residual_risks: The cycle pattern language and both total and maximal irredundance sequences are pre-existing (OEIS 2017); their independent novelty is expressly excluded.
An unindexed equivalent statement about true-twin expansions or lexicographic-product super domination may exist.
The 2018 maximal-irredundance paper was not fully available at the inspected source; the examined parts do not resolve every potential implication.

The cross-parameter mapping could be seen as a direct consequence of fundamental closed-private-neighborhood definitions; significance therefore depends on its all-configuration and all-coefficient product scope rather than on proof length.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-base correspondence classifies all super dominating sets and all inclusion-minimal super dominating sets of G[K_m] by the entire irredundance complex of G, and transfers all cardinality coefficients. A constant-size cyclic transfer and closed minimum-set multiplicity are concrete infinite-family consequences. This is stronger than earlier scalar bounds and known ordinary-cycle counts, which are acknowledged and not presented as independently new.
